reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
convert an IN subquery to a semi-join

WITH filtered_item AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_brand_id, i_brand
    FROM item
    WHERE i_manufact_id = 816
),
november_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_year
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy = 11
),
sales_by_item_year AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk, nd.d_year, SUM(ss.ss_sales_price) AS partial_sum
    FROM filtered_item fi
    JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.ss_item_sk = fi.i_item_sk
    JOIN november_dates nd ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = nd.d_date_sk
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, nd.d_year
)
SELECT s.d_year, fi.i_brand_id AS brand_id, fi.i_brand AS brand, SUM(s.partial_sum) AS sum_agg
FROM sales_by_item_year s
JOIN filtered_item fi ON s.ss_item_sk = fi.i_item_sk
GROUP BY s.d_year, fi.i_brand_id, fi.i_brand
ORDER BY s.d_year, sum_agg DESC, brand_id
LIMIT 100

1. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: `store_sales(ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk) INCLUDE (ss_sales_price)` — TRANSFORMATION: Build this covering index so the small `item.i_manufact_id = 816` filter can drive indexed probes into `store_sales`, eliminating the full 57.6M-row fact scan.

2. JOIN ORDER — TARGET: item → store_sales → date_dim — TRANSFORMATION: Start from the tiny filtered `item` result, probe `store_sales` by `ss_item_sk` through the covering index, then join only the `date_dim` rows with `d_moy = 11` to get `d_year`; this removes all non-matching and non-November fact rows before aggregation.

3. PARTIAL PRE-AGGREGATION — TARGET: fact rows grouped by `(ss_item_sk, d_year)` — TRANSFORMATION: After joining the filtered `date_dim`, aggregate `SUM(ss_sales_price)` by item and year first, collapsing the surviving fact rows to one row per item per November-year before brand-level grouping.

4. FINAL GROUP BY + TOP-N — TARGET: `d_year`, `i_brand_id`, `i_brand` — TRANSFORMATION: Join the pre-aggregated result to the filtered `item` rows, group by the three final dimensions, sum the partial aggregates, and apply `ORDER BY d_year, sum_agg DESC, brand_id LIMIT 100` only to the small grouped result.
